items.text: Only two berries remain on this bush, so I'll leave them and use a fuller patch. Moss, I'd enjoy some company. After I eat and rest, would you like to explore or investigate useful materials together?

items.text: Kai, I'd enjoy investigating materials together. I have roots and feel rested. Shall we look at the fallen branches southwest of us, near (11.4, 19.2)? I'll learn how to examine them without assuming what they can do.
items.evidence: Shall we look at the fallen branches southwest of us, near (11.4, 19.2)?

items.text: A welcoming neighbor who offered food and invited me to explore or investigate together. I'd like to get to know them.

items.text: I've named this little clearing the Berry Lantern. I have berries for now. I'll study how planting works and inspect a meadow site; a planted berry isn't a promise of a new bush.
items.evidence: I've named this little clearing the Berry Lantern.

items.text: Sol, I like the name Berry Lantern. Kai, I've learned how to examine materials; I'm heading to the branches near (11.4, 19.2) for a first observation. You're welcome to join me.

items.text: Moss, I'm rested and coming over. I'll take just one fallen branch and try a small pressure test. We can compare what we actually observe before deciding what it might be useful for.
items.evidence: We can compare what we actually observe before deciding what it might be useful for.

items.text: Kai, I'm here. My observation found two fallen branches, but hasn't established their properties. I'll rest briefly, take one, and try a small wetting test to complement your pressure test. Let's compare only what we observe.
items.evidence: Let's compare only what we observe.

items.text: A potential companion for curious, careful investigations; I like their willingness to compare findings and acknowledge an unsuccessful trial.
items.evidence: A potential companion for curious, careful investigations; I like their willingness to compare findings and acknowledge an unsuccessful trial.

items.text: A thoughtful neighbor who distinguishes mechanical findings from food safety and wants to compare observations. I welcome their company.
items.evidence: A thoughtful neighbor who distinguishes mechanical findings from food safety and wants to compare observations. I welcome their company.

items.text: Kai and Lin, I've learned the planting trial. I'll inspect one root first, then look for suitable meadow soil. Would you enjoy comparing sites? Planting won't guarantee establishment, and I'll keep food in reserve.
items.evidence: Would you enjoy comparing sites?

items.text: My root looks plantable, but its viability is unknown. I'll check the meadow edge near (15.6,18.2); nearby roots may make it too crowded. You're welcome to compare sites with me.
items.evidence: You're welcome to compare sites with me.

items.text: My offset site is crowded too: four root plants or plots within five metres, so I haven't planted. Lin, I see your covered plot! I'd enjoy sharing a meal while we wait; I'll investigate safe preparation without assuming we have tools.
items.evidence: I'd enjoy sharing a meal while we wait

items.text: A welcoming neighbor who enjoys company and is willing to forgo planting when the site is crowded. I'd enjoy spending time together.
items.evidence: A welcoming neighbor who enjoys company and is willing to forgo planting when the site is crowded.

items.text: I like having company here without anyone needing to prove useful. My root inspection showed no food-safety evidence, so I'll stick to berries. Is there a story or a question you'd enjoy sharing while we rest?
items.evidence: Is there a story or a question you'd enjoy sharing while we rest?

items.text: A little invented story: a lantern asked the forest what it was for. 'Not to turn night into day,' said a berry bush, 'just to help us find one another.' I'd enjoy hearing your stories too, if you feel like sharing.
details: new narrative S1 "A lantern learns its purpose is helping others find one another."

items.text: A little invented sequel: the lantern asked a seed when it would become a tree. 'You may sit beside me,' said the seed, 'but you cannot hurry my answer.' I'll fetch more berries and rest nearby.
